draft.title: Rights and responsibilities
card: Right
something a person is entitled to. For example, a consumer has the right to be told the truth about a product.
Responsibility
something a person is expected to do. For example, a consumer should read the details of a product before buying it.
Consumers and businesses both have rights and responsibilities. A business has the right to be paid for what it sells. It also has a responsibility to describe its products honestly.
A right is what you can expect from others. A responsibility is what others can expect from you.
draft.remember: Rights are what you are entitled to. Responsibilities are what you are expected to do.

a.q: Which of these is a responsibility of a consumer?
opts: Checking the price before paying for an item
Being given honest information about an item
Being able to buy an item that is safe to use
Being told the true price of an item by the seller
a.why: Checking the price is something a consumer is expected to do, so it is a responsibility. The other three are things a consumer is entitled to receive from the seller, so they are rights.
a.clue: Which one is something the consumer does, not something they receive?

b.q: Jaden buys a skateboard from a shop in Hobart. The shop gives him a true description of it. Which sentence is correct?
opts: The shop met its responsibility and Jaden's right was met
The shop used its right and Jaden met his responsibility
The shop met its responsibility and Jaden used his right
The shop used its right and Jaden's responsibility was met
b.why: The shop is expected to describe its products honestly, so that is its responsibility. Jaden is entitled to honest information, so his right was met. The other options swap who is entitled and who is expected to act.
b.clue: Who is expected to act, and who is entitled to receive?

a.best: Checking the price before paying for an item

b.best: The shop met its responsibility and Jaden's right was met

problems.detail: The right option is the only one written as an action ('Checking...'). The other three all begin with 'Being...', so a student can pick it from the grammar alone without knowing the idea. The clue ('something the consumer does, not something they receive') makes this giveaway stronger.

The distractor 'The shop met its responsibility and Jaden used his right' is very close to the right answer. The difference between 'used his right' and 'his right was met' is a fine one for Year 7. Also, because Jaden 'buys' the skateboard, a student could argue that the shop used its right to be paid and Jaden met a responsibility by paying. That makes 'The shop used its right and Jaden met his responsibility' arguable under a loose reading.

Using a right she has as a consumer

Using a right the business has
